items.title: Delete objects in bulk and report their checksums

goal.title: Delete objects in bulk and report their checksums
criteria: Deleting a list of keys removes exactly those objects from the stand-in and leaves every other object in place.
Deleting more than 1,000 keys is split into several requests, and every key is removed.
Deleting a key that does not exist is not an error.
Refused credentials, a server error, or keys the store refuses individually are reported, naming the refused keys.
A listing reports, for each key, the checksum of its bytes, and an object rewritten with different bytes is listed with a different checksum.
Existing listing callers see the same keys and paging as before.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/spaces/client.go:240-260 (Delete) and deleteBatch at :264-316 send the keys in one POST ?delete body; spacestest/spacestest.go:276-324 (serveDelete) removes only the listed keys. delete_test.go:18-32 (TestDeleteRemovesExactlyTheKeysGiven) seeds five objects, deletes three, and asserts Keys("") is exactly the two others.

client.go:217 sets deleteBatch = 1000 and client.go:242-255 loops over keys in chunks of min(len, 1000), one request per chunk. delete_test.go:34-52 (TestDeleteSplitsIntoBatchesOfAThousand) deletes 2500 keys and asserts Requests("POST","?delete") == 3 and that all 2500 are gone; the server also enforces the 1000 cap at spacestest.go:298.

spacestest.go:312-319 deletes only keys that exist and never reports a missing key as an error; client.go:299-315 treats an empty result as success. delete_test.go:54-70 (TestDeleteMissingKeyAndNoKeysAreNotErrors) deletes a missing key alongside an existing one and asserts err == nil.

Per-key refusals are met: client.go:221-233 DeleteError carries Failed map[key]code and its Error() names the first refused key (delete_test.go:114-140 checks k0001 and k1200 AccessDenied). But whole-request refusals and server errors are not: client.go:296-297 returns responseError(resp) and client.go:292-294 and 244-246 only add a wrapper message 'spaces: delete N keys', and errors.go:8-12 defines *Error with Status, Code and Message only, with no key field. So refused credentials or a 500 are reported without naming the keys they applied to. delete_test.go:86-112 (TestDeleteFailuresAreReported) checks status and code only, never the keys. Needed: the batch's keys must be attached to the error for the credential and server-error paths (e.g. a wrapper carrying the keys, or an added Keys field) and asserted in a test.

client.go:25-30 and 153-162 add ListPage.ETags, filled from each Contents ETag with quotes trimmed (client.go:203-208). spacestest.go:236-247 and 264-265 list each object's ETag as the hex MD5 of its bytes (newObject at :39-42, set on every PUT at :186 and SetObject at :354). delete_test.go:147-195 (TestListReportsEachObjectsChecksum) checks the MD5 of each listed key and that a rewrite with new bytes reports the MD5 of the new bytes, which differs from the old one.

client.go:153-162 keeps Keys and Next unchanged in meaning; the List body at :191-212 still decodes the same Contents, IsTruncated and NextContinuationToken fields and sets Next only when truncated. The ETag field is additive. spacestest.go:232-270 (serveList) keeps the same prefix, token and page-size logic. delete_test.go:147-195 pages through List with PageSize(1) and checks that Keys and Next behave as before. client_test.go is not in the diff, so its existing List assertions are unchanged, and the goal's go test run passed.

criteria: Deleting a list of keys removes exactly those objects from the stand-in and leaves every other object in place.
Deleting more than 1,000 keys is split into several requests, and every key is removed.
Deleting a key that does not exist is not an error.
Refused credentials, a server error, or keys the store refuses individually are reported, naming the refused keys.
A listing reports, for each key, the checksum of its bytes, and an object rewritten with different bytes is listed with a different checksum.
Existing listing callers see the same keys and paging as before.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/spaces/client.go:255-280 Delete sends each key in a DeleteObjects request; spacestest/spacestest.go serveDelete (diff ~L316-364) deletes only the listed keys from s.objects. internal/spaces/delete_test.go:18-32 TestDeleteRemovesExactlyTheKeysGiven seeds 5 objects, deletes 3, and asserts Keys('') == the 2 untouched keys.

client.go:215 const deleteBatch = 1000; Delete loops over keys[:min(len,1000)] (client.go:257-275). delete_test.go:34-52 TestDeleteSplitsIntoBatchesOfAThousand deletes 2500 keys and asserts exactly 3 POST ?delete requests and only the one non-target key left.

serveDelete removes via Go map delete, which is a no-op for a missing key, and reports no error entry for it (spacestest.go serveDelete loop). delete_test.go:54-70 TestDeleteMissingKeyAndNoKeysAreNotErrors deletes a missing key alongside a present one and asserts err == nil.

client.go:219-246 DeleteError carries Failed map (key->S3 code) and Err; Error() names the count and first refused key with its code. Whole-request failures (refused creds, 500, bad digest, transport) set every carried key in Failed (client.go:261-269); per-key refusals come from the response <Error> entries (client.go:328-334). delete_test.go:104-158 covers refused credentials, InternalError, InvalidDigest, a closed server, a request failure naming all 1500 keys, and per-key AccessDenied naming k0001 and k1200 (160-186).

client.go:152-208: ListPage gains ETags map populated from each <Contents><ETag> (quotes trimmed). The doc comment (client.go:156-160) states it is the hex MD5 of the bytes for single-part PUTs; grep found no multipart upload path in internal/spaces, so every object this package writes qualifies. spacestest.go newObject computes MD5 on every write, and SetObject/PUT both use it. delete_test.go:193-241 TestListReportsEachObjectsChecksum checks each key's MD5 and that a rewrite with different bytes lists a different checksum. Caveat: the checksum is S3's ETag, not a checksum the client computes, so it holds only for objects written without multipart or SSE-C; the code documents this.

client.go:168-212: List still builds Keys in the same order, sets Next only when IsTruncated, and sends the same query (list-type, prefix, continuation-token). The only change is the added ETags field and the ETag element in the decode struct, which existing callers ignore. spacestest.go serveList still sorts and pages the same way; the ETag element is omitempty. The existing client_test.go list tests were not changed, and the verification summary reports go test ./internal/... passing.

items.title: Purge the bucket CDN through the DigitalOcean API

goal.title: Purge the bucket CDN through the DigitalOcean API
criteria: A purge sends exactly the requested paths, wildcards included, to the CDN endpoint whose origin is the bucket, with the token.
When the account has no CDN endpoint for the bucket, the purge reports that distinctly and purges nothing.
A refused token, or a failing or unreachable API, is reported as an error that never contains the token.
The stand-in records every purge's paths, and refuses requests without the right token.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/spaces/cdn.go:72-94 (Purge) sends paths[:n] unchanged, in batches of at most 50, as the JSON body {"files": [...]} to DELETE /v2/cdn/endpoints/<id>/cache. The id comes from endpointID (cdn.go:98-129), which matches e.Origin against c.Origin with strings.EqualFold. NewCDN (cdn.go:55-66) sets Origin to <bucket>.<host>. do (cdn.go:133-170) sets Authorization: Bearer <token>. Wildcards pass through untouched, and cdn_test.go:43-58 checks that the fake receives exactly the paths asked for, including 'images/en/me/me01/*'.

cdn.go:126 returns the sentinel ErrNoCDN when the endpoint pages run out with no endpoint whose origin matches (cdn.go:125 also stops on an empty page). Purge returns that error at cdn.go:76-78 before any DELETE is sent, so nothing is purged. The error is distinct and testable with errors.Is. cdn_test.go:92-102 (TestPurgeWithoutAnEndpointForTheBucket) sets a different origin and asserts ErrNoCDN with zero purges recorded.

do (cdn.go:133-170) returns a *CDNError built from the API's id and message for non-2xx responses, and both fields pass through scrubText (cdn.go:165, 180-185). Transport errors go through scrub (cdn.go:150-152, 172-178), which replaces the token in the error text. Purge and endpointID wrap these errors without adding the token. The request URL carries no token. cdn_test.go:128-158 covers a wrong token (401), a failing API (500) and a closed server (transport error), and checks that none of the error texts contain the token.

spacestest/cdn.go:39-44 checks the bearer token before anything else and answers 401 without recording. spacestest/cdn.go:79-82 appends body.Files to c.purges for each valid DELETE on the bucket's endpoint, and Purges() (spacestest/cdn.go:89-97) returns them in order. cdn_test.go:160-178 checks that requests without the token get 401 and that no purge is recorded. Note: a DELETE aimed at another endpoint id gets a 404 and is not recorded, and a purge with an empty files list gets a 422 and is not recorded. Both fit the stand-in's stated scope of recording the bucket endpoint's purges.

goal.title: Clear the card stores
criteria: Clearing everything leaves no card data files in the cache directory and no objects under the card data prefix in the stand-in Spaces.
Clearing one set removes its card list and every one of its cards from disk and from the stand-in, and keeps the set list and every other set's data.
Sets whose ids share a beginning with the cleared set (for example `sv03` and `sv03.5`) are untouched.
Each store reports how many entries it removed. A shared-store failure is reported while the local tier is still cleared.
A clear reaches the shared store even when lookups are currently skipping it after a failure.
Stores that cannot clear, and every existing caller of the stores, keep working unchanged.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: Disk clear-all removes sets.json, set-index-v2.json, and every file in sets/ and cards/ then RemoveAll on both dirs: /home/nicj/code/github.com/nicholasjackson/tcgreplay/.spektacular/worktrees/20261104090640-a5a74fab-admin-cache-clearing/tcgreplay/internal/cards/store.go:177-191. Spaces clear-all lists the whole tcgdex/ prefix (spacesprefix) and deletes every key: internal/cards/spacesstore.go:65-97. Test clear_store_test.go:69-97 and 108-133 checks the disk dir and Keys("tcgdex/") are empty after clear-all. Images live under images/ in the bucket (images.go:21-23, 404), not in the cache directory, and the cache directory holds nothing else card-related in the non-test code.

Disk one-set clear removes sets/<id>.json and cards/<id>-*.json only: store.go:193-204. Spaces one-set clear lists exactly tcgdex/sets/<id>.json and tcgdex/cards/<id>- and deletes them: spacesstore.go:66-71, 84-95. Set list (sets.json, tcgdex/sets.json) is never in those prefixes. Test clear_store_test.go:55-67 and 108-121 asserts the sets list and other sets survive.

The separator rule is in internal/cards/scope.go:14-15 and 33-40: the key match requires "cards/<id>-", so sv03 does not match cards/sv03.5-001 or sets/sv03.5. Disk uses prefix safeName(id)+"-" at store.go:196-201, and Spaces uses tcgdex/cards/<id>- and tcgdex/sets/<id>.json at spacesstore.go:68-69. Tests scope_test.go:21-25 (sv03 vs sv03.5) and clear_store_test.go:55-67 cover it.

Each store returns a TierReport with a Removed count: disk at store.go:170-176 and 193-205, shared at spacesstore.go:84-95 (Removed = keys minus DeleteError.Failed). A shared failure does not stop the local clear: tieredStore.Clear at tiered.go:116-133 clears shared, appends its reports, then always runs the local clear. The listing error path returns early only inside spacesStore.Clear, and the tiered method continues. Test clear_store_test.go:168-188 asserts the shared error is reported and disk removed everything.

tieredStore.Clear at internal/cards/tiered.go:116-133 calls the shared store's Clear without consulting t.skip(). It only calls t.ok() when no shared report has an error (tiered.go:124-126), so a failed clear does not trip the skip. Test clear_store_test.go:201-224 trips the breaker with a failed Get, then asserts the clear issues one POST ?delete request, removes the 3 keys, and lifts the skip.

The Store interface is unchanged (store.go:32-37, Get and Put only). Clear is an optional interface found by type assertion (scope.go:68-72), so plainStore and other stores are unaffected; clear_store_test.go:251-266 covers a non-clearer local tier. Existing callers in cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:255 (NewTieredStore(db.Store, NewSpacesStore(sc))) and internal/cards/cards.go:201-218 are unchanged in the diff. The spaces.ListPage change is additive (ETags field, List signature unchanged) in internal/spaces/client.go. Verification reports go vet, gofmt and go test ./... as passing. Scope note, not a criterion verdict: the diff also touches internal/spaces/client.go, internal/spaces/spacestest/spacestest.go and the untracked internal/spaces/cdn.go, cdn_test.go, delete_test.go and spacestest/cdn.go, none of which are in this item's file list, so the scope rule may be violated.

items.title: Clear the card database and name sets

goal.title: Clear the card database and name sets
criteria: A set named by its decklist code (such as `MEG`), by its id (such as `me01`) or by its id in another case names the same set. A name that matches no set is refused, even after the set list has been refreshed.
After a clear of everything, the next card lookup makes one request to the card source and returns its current data, and deck codes resolve again through freshly fetched set data.
After a clear of one set, a lookup of a card in that set makes one request to the card source, while a lookup of a cached card in another set makes none.
After a clear, the cached-only lookup still returns a cleared card's previous copy without any network request, and returns the fresh copy once the background fetch completes.
If the card source is down after a clear, card lookups return the previous copy with no error.
A fetch or set-data build that started before a clear does not put pre-clear data back into memory.
A recent failed or missed lookup inside the cleared scope does not stop the next lookup from asking the card source.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/cards/clear.go:21-60 SetID resolves a name by case-insensitive TCGdex id (EqualFold over cat.setIDs), then normCode (cards.go:695, upper case plus codeAliases) through setAliases and cat.setIndex, which is built from the set's official abbreviation (catalog.go:199-210). A miss calls refreshSetList once per RetryAfter per name (missAllowed, catalog.go:426) and retries; a name still unmatched returns ErrUnknownSet (clear.go:50-51). TestSetIDNamesASetByCodeOrID in clear_test.go:53-92 checks MEG, meg, me01, ME01 and ' me01 ' all give me01, and that XYZ is refused after one refresh.

Clear(Scope{}) (clear.go:74-115) clears the store (diskStore.Clear store.go:427-470 removes sets.json, set-index-v2.json, sets/, cards/; tieredStore.Clear tiered.go:490-507 clears shared then local), marks memory cards cleared, sets c.cat=nil and resets tracker.failed/bg/miss. The next Card goes loadCard (cards.go:472-494): store miss, recentlyFailed is false, shared() makes one source request. Resolve goes ensureCatalog (catalog.go:47-80) and buildCatalog reloads sets from source since the store is empty. TestClearEverythingRefetchesCardsAndSets (clear_test.go:98-145) asserts one /cards/me01-001 request, one /sets and one /sets/me01 request, and the new data. Caveat, not a verdict: shared() (cards.go:372) writes the store with no generation check, so a pre-clear fetch still in flight can write pre-clear data to disk after the clear. That race is not covered by any test.

Scope.Key (scope.go:35-40) matches only sets/<id> and cards/<id>- keys, so sv03 does not match sv03.5. Clear(Scope{Set}) (clear.go:84-105) marks only in-scope memory entries cleared and forgets only in-scope tracker.failed/bg keys. diskStore.Clear (store.go:441-469) removes only that set's files. The lookup of an in-scope card makes one request (loadCard path, cards.go:472-494). A cached card in another set is served from memory with no request (cards.go:454-456, cleared is false). TestClearOneSetLeavesOtherSets (clear_test.go:149-176) asserts me01-001 gets 2 requests in total and sv1-001 gets 1 request.

Cached (cards.go:499-524) returns the cleared entry's old copy at once and calls warmCleared, a background refresh (fresh.go:118-135), without waiting on the network. refreshCard captures gen before starting, and remember (cards.go:272-286) accepts the fresh copy because gen still matches and a cleared entry gives way to a fetched one. TestCachedServesClearedCopyThenFreshOne (clear_test.go:181-210) asserts the old copy within 500ms while the fetch is delayed by 1s, then the fresh copy (HP 80) after waitBackground.

Card (cards.go:446-468): a cleared entry goes to loadCard; when that errors and ok is true, it returns old.card with a nil error (cards.go:461-465). Offline also returns old.card (cards.go:454). TestClearedCardSurvivesSourceOutage (clear_test.go:212-235) covers unreachable, failing and offline sources and expects the old copy with no error.

remember (cards.go:272-286) returns without storing when c.gen != gen, so a card load or background refresh begun before a clear never writes memory. publish (catalog.go:84-90) and update (catalog.go:257-304) also check gen, and refreshSet, refreshSetList and sweep capture gen first (catalog.go:260, 276-283, 378-380). ensureCatalog's flight key includes the generation (catalog.go:59-60). TestCatalogBuildBegunBeforeClearIsNotKept (clear_test.go:240-281) and TestCardFetchBegunBeforeClearIsNotKept (clear_test.go:285-322) both assert nothing pre-clear reaches memory. The disk write noted under criterion 2 is not memory, so it does not affect this criterion.

Clear (clear.go:92-108) deletes tracker.failed and tracker.bg entries whose keys are in scope (all of them on a whole clear), and sets tracker.miss = nil on every clear, so missAllowed (catalog.go:426-438) and recentlyFailed (fresh.go:58-63) no longer block the next lookup. TestClearForgetsRecentFailuresInScope (clear_test.go:324-366) covers a failed card and a missed number in scope, and expects the next lookups to ask the source.

items.title: Prove an open game survives a clear

goal.title: Prove an open game survives a clear
criteria: After everything is cleared, board reads of the open game still show every card's definition (name, HP, text, image), each read returning within a second.
A play on the game after the clear succeeds and behaves as before the clear.
Once background work settles, the game's cards have been fetched again from the card source.
With the card source down during and after the clear, the game still shows and plays its cards with no error.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/game/clear_test.go:96-121 (TestOpenGameSurvivesAClear): client.Clear(ctx, cards.Scope{}) at line 108, then inside quick(t, "board reads after the clear", ...) (quick fails at >=1s, internal/game/cardlock_test.go:84-91) defsShown reads every def via client.Cached and compares Name, HP, Text() and Image against the pre-clear snapshot (lines 115-119). clear_test.go:144-172 does the same with Name-less Text/Image checks under the source-down test. Cached returns the cleared in-memory copy without blocking (internal/cards/cards.go:499-508, warmCleared is background).

internal/game/clear_test.go:63-90 (playOn) runs after the clear in both tests (lines 122, 163): it reads both seats' View, then PlaceActive(state.P1, state.ActorHuman, basic) with t.Fatalf on error (line 84) and asserts the Active spot holds the played Riolu (tst-1) card (lines 87-89). Caveat: no pre-clear play is run for side-by-side comparison; 'as before' is judged as the same play succeeding with the same resulting state.

internal/game/clear_test.go:124-137: after playOn, waitFor(t, 5*time.Second, "cards fetched again", ...) waits until src.count("/cards/"+d) > 0 for every def and until client.Cached("tst-4") contains the corrected text; then each def's fetch count is asserted to be exactly 1 (lines 133-137). The liveSource hit counter is in internal/game/clear_test.go:186-191 and internal/game/spacescache_test.go:20-69. The background warm path is internal/cards/cards.go:499-508 (Cached -> warmCleared) and internal/cards/fresh.go:316-334 (refreshCard).

internal/game/clear_test.go:147-172 (TestOpenGameSurvivesAClearWithTheSourceDown): src.Close() at line 151 before client.Clear at line 154, so the source is down during and after the clear. Board reads via quick and Cached (lines 155-162) compare the old copies with no error path; playOn (line 163) fails the test on any play error; client.Card for each def (lines 164-170) must return a non-nil card with nil error and the old text, as internal/cards/cards.go:446-471 returns old.card when the load fails and a cleared copy exists. Final View at line 171 ignores its return value, but the earlier playOn views do check errors (line 67).

items.title: Version image copies by their content

goal.title: Version image copies by their content
criteria: A copied image is answered with its CDN address, its card source fallback, and a version. An image without a copy has no version.
Copying the same bytes again gives the same version. Copying different bytes gives a different one.
After a restart, an image found in the bucket gets the same version it had before the restart.
An image whose two files' checksums are not both known counts as not copied, as a half copy does.
Answers still never wait on the network.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/cards/images.go:171-199: Image now returns (image, fallback, version). A copied image (ic.known[rel] present, line 181) returns the CDN address ic.Public+"/"+ImagePrefix+rel, the source as fallback, and the stored content version (line 183). An uncopied image returns the source with fallback "" and version "" on every uncopied path (lines 174, 177, 188, 191, 199). internal/cards/images_version_test.go:72-94 (TestImageCopyIsAnsweredWithItsContentVersion) checks each part. Note: internal/webui/server.go discards the version (`img, fb, _ =`); that wiring is outside this item's scope.

images.go:149-165: imageVersion is the first 12 hex chars of SHA-256(lowETag + "\n" + highETag), and the copier takes each ETag as MD5 of the uploaded bytes (images.go:420-421, copyOne). Same bytes give the same MD5 and so the same version; changed bytes in either file change the MD5 and so the version. images_version_test.go:96-121 (TestImageVersionFollowsTheBytes) covers the same-bytes and new-bytes cases; TestImageVersionFormula pins the formula.

images.go:254-281: loadKnown lists ImagePrefix with ETags (list passes page.ETags[k], line 337-338) and marks each whole image known at versionOf(fs), the same formula as the copier. The ETags are parsed in internal/spaces/client.go (ListPage.ETags, List reads <ETag>). images_version_test.go:123-137 (TestImageVersionSurvivesARestart) checks the version is unchanged after a restart.

images.go:163-165: versionOf returns "" unless both ImageFiles have a non-empty ETag. loadKnown (images.go:266-274) records an image as known only when versionOf is non-empty; otherwise it goes to partial and is not known. copyOne (images.go:431-434) returns before marking known when versionOf is "". Image answers such an image with no version (images.go:185-199). images_version_test.go:154-190 (TestImageWithoutBothChecksumsCountsAsNotCopied) checks both the listing path and the self-listing path.

images.go:171-200: Image does only a map lookup under ic.mu, a bounded in-memory check, and a non-blocking select send on ic.queue (default branch at line 196). It makes no network call. imageVersion/versionOf are pure CPU work. images_version_test.go:192-209 (TestImageAnswersWithVersionsNeverWaitOnTheNetwork) holds the server with Hang() and checks Image still answers quickly with versions. Caveat, not a verdict issue: images_version_test.go is an untracked file outside the scope's two named files.

items.title: Clear image copies and purge the CDN

goal.title: Clear image copies and purge the CDN
criteria: Clearing one set deletes every copy of that set's images from the stand-in, and keeps every other set's copies.
Clearing everything deletes every image copy.

From the moment a clear starts, images in scope are answered with the card source's address. No copy in scope is made until the clear has finished, and the next view after it copies the current art again.

With a purge client, the stand-in DigitalOcean API records a purge of the cleared set's image paths, or of all image paths for a full clear. Without one, the clear completes and reports that the CDN was not purged.
A failed delete or purge is reported, and the copies in scope are still no longer pointed at.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/cards/images.go Clear (around lines 741-765): keys are kept only when !s.All() and s.Image(rest[:i]) matches, i.e. segs[2]==set (scope.go:44-50), so only that set's objects are deleted via ic.Spaces.Delete. known/partial/failed entries for the set are dropped (images.go Clear, the known/partial/failed loops). Other sets' keys are not in the delete list. images_clear_test.go TestImageClearOfOneSet asserts 4 removed, the me01 copies gone, sv1 and swsh12.5 copies kept (2 files each) and the purge of images/en/me/me01/*; it passed.

images.go Clear: when s.All() every key under ImagePrefix is appended (the set filter is skipped because of !s.All()), and paths = [ImagePrefix+"*"]. The delete at images.go (images.Removed = len(keys); ic.Spaces.Delete) covers all of them, including stray non-copy objects under images/. images_clear_test.go TestImageClearOfEverything asserts srv.Keys(ImagePrefix) is empty after the clear (9 removed, including images/stray.txt) and that every swsh/sv/me image answers the source.

images.go Clear appends s to ic.clearing under ic.mu before any listing or delete. Image() returns (src, "", "") for inScopes(ic.clearing, rel) before consulting known or queuing (images.go Image, the inScopes(ic.clearing) branch). handle() sets skip when inScopes(ic.clearing, rel) and only marks copying[rel] when not skipping. Clear waits (ic.idle.Wait loop over ic.copying) until no in-scope copy is under way, then drops known/partial/failed for the scope, so no in-scope copy is made during the clear. The scope is removed from clearing only in the deferred function at the end, so the next Image after the clear sees known deleted and queues a fresh copy (copyOne). Tests: TestImageClearHoldsOffCopiesThenCopiesTheCurrentArt (source answered during clear, PUT count unchanged, new version after re-copy) and TestImageClearWaitsForACopyUnderWay both exist and passed.

images.go Clear, cdn switch: a set clear purges images/<lang>/<serie>/<set>/* per directory found (dirs map), and a full clear purges ["images/*"]; the purge goes through ic.CDN.Purge, which is internal/spaces/cdn.go CDN.Purge (DELETE /v2/cdn/endpoints/{id}/cache with the files). The stand-in is internal/spaces/spacestest/cdn.go (NewCDN, Purges, SetFail). images_clear_test.go TestImageClearOfOneSet asserts cdn.Purges() == [[images/en/me/me01/*]]; TestImageClearOfEverything asserts [[images/*]]. Without a purge client (ic.CDN == nil) cdn.Err = ErrCDNNotConfigured and the log says "CDN not purged (no TCGREPLAY_SPACES_CDN_TOKEN)"; TestImageClearWithoutAPurgeClient checks both. Caveat, not a verdict change: no production code sets ImageCache.CDN or calls ImageCache.Clear (grep finds ImageCache.Clear only in tests; cards/clear.go Client.Clear does not call the image cache; cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go hostedCardDB sets no CDN), so the admin clear path does not reach this yet. Also when a set has no copies, no purge is sent ("nothing to purge"), which is the expected reading of 'the cleared set's image paths'.

images.go Clear: a failed listing or delete sets images.Err; the delete failure is reported through images.Err and Removed is reduced by the DeleteError.Failed count (internal/cards/images.go Clear and internal/spaces/client.go Delete/DeleteError). A failed purge sets cdn.Err, which is returned in the report ("error: ..." in the log). The copies are no longer pointed at as the clear returns: known, partial and failed for the scope were deleted up front, and Image() answers the source while the scope is in clearing and afterwards finds no known entry (images.go Clear loops; TestImageClearWithDeletesRefused asserts Image returns the source after a refused delete, and TestImageClearReportsAFailedPurge asserts the copies are gone after a failed purge). Caveat: the leftover objects that could not be deleted are added to ic.unsure, and the next view's copyOne lists them and can re-mark the image known (images.go copyOne, versionOf(have)), so the cache may point at undeleted old copies again after a later view. TestImageClearWithDeletesRefused checks the no-overwrite and LIST behaviour there but does not assert against re-pointing. The immediate criterion holds.
